analysis: All four changed files are documentation only; no executable code, workflow or config changed. The security-relevant change is docs/architecture/security/encryption.md head lines 110-118. It documents that ad hoc signed builds get no persistent cache key, so SSD stores are refused with key_unavailable unless an ephemeral key is explicitly allowed. It also documents a DEBUG-only DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE path (SSDDebugCacheKeyFile.swift) that derives the KEK from an operator-created 0600 file. The text states that this key material is not Secure Enclave-rooted and that release builds do not contain the path. This touches T-041 (the cache at-rest posture), which says the KEK is SE-rooted and that KEK wipe is the cryptographic purge. The docs disclose the DEBUG exception, so there is no misleading claim. The T-041 text does not mention the new key source, and the existing T-041 mitigation text assumes an SE-rooted KEK. That is a minor threat-model documentation gap. The new code file is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not check whether release builds really exclude the debug path (for example via #if DEBUG) or whether ephemeral-key permission can be enabled in production. This is an unverified contract, not a finding. The docs/design/glm53-flash-native.md addition describes glm5_next as excluded from EngineV2SupportedModels and not qualified, and states that cache identity and encryption protections must be preserved. It authorizes no rollout. docs/developer/build.md adds test and build guidance only, and the README change is an index entry. I found no regressions. The remaining integration question is whether SSDDebugCacheKeyFile.swift is compiled out of release builds and whether the ephemeral-key opt-in is unreachable in production. That code was not supplied.
